note: Engine cases for the DATE-LITERAL exhibit (ymd-dates.l4, spec §15.4).
WHAT THESE COVER: that a date written the way `daydate.l4` recommends --
`YMD y m d`, ISO order, bounds-checked -- reaches a real engine as a real
FEEL date, in all three positions the exhibit puts one: a boxed literal
body (`commencement`, `the appointed day`, `the transition day`), a
decision-table CELL endpoint (`the regime that applies`), and a law-time
interval endpoint (`the filing fee`). Before the fold, every one of those
was raw L4 that neither engine would parse.
TWO INDEPENDENT DATE AXES, and the cases separate them: `the_application
_date` is the date the CASE is about, `RULES_EFFECTIVE_DATE` is the date
the LAW is about. Cases A-G move them together because that is the cheap
way to straddle both tables' seams at once; case H moves them apart, so a
lowering that confused the two would fail there and only there.
EVERY SEAM IS STRADDLED BY A DAY-OF / DAY-BEFORE PAIR, which is what pins
the closed-low / open-high convention:
* 2026-01-01 (both tables)       A + B
* 2024-02-29 (the regime table)  C + D
* 1983-01-01 (both tables)       E + F
Delete a pair and an off-by-one on that interval passes green.
2024-02-29 IS THE POINT OF CASE C. A leap day is the cheapest proof the
fold consults a calendar rather than range-checking three numbers, and it
is also the argument-order guard: read little-endian, `YMD 2024 2 29`
would be nonsense (day 2024) and would not fold at all, so a transposed
implementation cannot reach this expectation by accident. Its refusing
sibling `YMD 2023 2 29` -- 2023 was not a leap year -- is pinned in
not-ok/ymd-unfoldable-date.l4 and in jl4/tests/DmnExport.hs.
`{"$date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}` is the fixture vocabulary's only way to say
"this is a FEEL date"; both harnesses convert by declared type, never by
appearance (see KieDmnCheck.jsonToFeel's BigDecimal note).
ACTIVATION CONTRACT: every expected value below was derived from the L4
SOURCE, not from a DMN engine's own output -- a pin regenerated from the
thing it pins is vacuous. Measured 2026-08-02 with the built `l4` binary
on eight copies of ymd-dates.l4 whose two ASSUMEs were replaced by the
case's own values, each carrying
`#EVAL \`EVAL UNDER RULES EFFECTIVE AT\` (YMD y m d) <decision>` for all
six decisions. L4 answered `DATE OF 1, 1, 1983` / `DATE OF 29, 2, 2024` /
`DATE OF 1, 1, 2026` for the three constants in every case, which is the
same argument-order check from the evaluator's side.
WHAT THEY DO NOT COVER, so a green run is not read as more than it is:
the floor row's answer is an ASSUME bottom, which L4 refuses to evaluate.
Here it is an ordinary DMN input, and -1 is a sentinel chosen because no
real fee could be negative, so a floor-row hit is unmistakable in the
harness output (same device as gst-rate.cases.json).

cases.name: A. on the transition day (both axes)
B. the day before the transition day
C. on the appointed day, which is a leap day
D. the day before the appointed day
F. the day before commencement (both floor rows)
H. the two date axes pulled apart
